paper.title: Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Bandits with Unobserved Contexts

settings.name_in_paper: Federated linear contextual bandit with heterogeneous agents and unobserved contexts (context distribution available)
unmapped: Each of M agents has a fixed unobserved context vector c_i; only its distribution mu_i is observed; agent features are psi_{a,mu_i}=E[phi_{a,c_i}]
Reward parameter theta_a is arm-specific (disjoint per-arm linear models) shared across agents
Agents communicate with a central server periodically, sharing only estimates (federated)
Feature norms bounded below by ell > 0; the learner uses ell in its confidence widths (learner knows ell)
Regret measured against the optimal action given the context distribution mu_i, not the true context c_i
settings.definition_quote: Each agent $i\in [M]$ is a user in the system whose user profile is denoted by $c_i \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and all agents have the same action set $\A=[K]$. The context vector $c_i$ cannot be observed by the agent $i$ and only the context distribution $\mu_i$ is available. ... receive the reward $\yt =\langle\theta_{a_{i, t}}, \phi_{a_{i, t}, c_i} \rangle+ \eta_{i, t}$

algorithms.name: Fed-PECD (Federated Phased Elimination with Context Distribution)

bound.expression_latex: O\left( \frac{L}{\l} \sqrt{d K M T( \log (K( \log T) / \delta) + \min \{ d, \log M\})}\right)

symbols.ell: lower bound on feature vector norms, ell <= ||phi_{a,c_i}||_2

conditions: K = O(sqrt(T)) (used in the proof to obtain the stated rate)
tuning: f_p = c n^p with integers c, n > 1
alpha = min{sqrt(2 log(2MKH/delta)), sqrt(2 log(KH/delta) + d log(k e))}, k > 1 with kd >= 2 log(KH/delta) + d log(ke)

source.label: Thm
source.quote: Consider time horizon $T$ that consists of $H$ phases with $\fp = cn^p$, ... Then, with probability (w.p) at least $1 - \delta$ the cumulative regret of our algorithm scales in $O\left( \frac{L}{\l} \sqrt{d K M T( \log (K( \log T) / \delta) + \min \{ d, \log M\})}\right)$ and communication cost scales in $O\left( M d^2 K \log{T}\right)$.

results.notes: Regret is total over M agents, against the optimal action given psi (context distribution). Proof gives the more general O((L/ell) sqrt(dKM(log(K log T/delta)+min{d,log M}))(sqrt(T)+K)) and specialises to K=O(sqrt T). Paper's M mapped to N.

tuning: f_p = c n^p with integers c, n > 1
